length.text: Body about 1 m; up to about 1.6-2 m in total

diet.text: Frogs, skinks and other small reptiles, fish

overview.text: The Common (Green) Tree Snake is a slender, large-eyed, harmless snake of northern and eastern Australia and New Guinea. It is agile, climbs well and is a strong swimmer.

size.label: Adults
size.text: In a Queensland study, the body (without the tail) averaged about 1 m in females and 0.93 m in males. The total length can reach about 1.6 m, and some sources say up to 2 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Northern and eastern Australia - from the Kimberley across to Cape York and the Torres Strait and down the east coast into New South Wales - and Papua New Guinea.

habitat.text: Bushland, well-vegetated banks of rivers and creeks, rainforest edges and gardens with ponds.

behaviour.text: Active by day; it rests at night in hollow trees, logs, leaves or rock cracks. It is harmless to people but may bite or give off a smell if handled.

diet.text: Frogs, water skinks and other small reptiles and their eggs, small fish, small mammals and turtle hatchlings.

recognise.text: Very slender body with big eyes.
Active by day, often in trees.
